title: Layered Network Defense Reference
description: Interactive Mermaid layered architecture diagram showing defense in depth from the untrusted Internet down to internal datastores, with each layer labeled by the attack class it addresses and three cross-cutting concerns (IDS/IPS, encryption in transit, logging/SIEM).
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection"

educational.topic: Defense in depth and layered network architecture
learningObjectives: Describe the ordered layers of a defense-in-depth network architecture.
Match each defensive layer to the attack class it primarily addresses.
Explain why IDS/IPS, encryption in transit, and logging are cross-cutting concerns rather than single appliances.
educational.prerequisites: Basic familiarity with firewalls, subnets, and HTTP.

pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions in the lesson plan ask students to reason about which layer stops which attack and what survives a single-layer failure.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a single firewall is sufficient ('perimeter is enough').
Treating monitoring and encryption as one box rather than concerns that span every layer.
